paragraphs: Rav Chiyya bar Rav, who would reverse his father's words to his mother because she was quarrelsome: chapter HaBa Al Yevimto, 63a, near the end. Rav told his son Chiyya, “Seize the opportunity and bless”: Berakhot 53b, near the end; Nazir 66a, near the end. He was a sickly man: Avodah Zarah 31b. And Rav Giddel bar Minyomi. Rav Huna—whether he was greater than he; see there. Rav Huna bar Chinena, in his name. R. Chiyya bar Ashi taught him before Rav: Eruvin 47a. Rav Chinena bar Shelamya, his teacher. And Rav Chilkiyah bar Tuvya. Rav Chanan bar Rava taught him before Rav. Rav Yehudah taught him before Rav: Eruvin 2b, 11a, 14a. He and R. Yehoshua ben Levi disagree: Sukkah 48a. Rabbah bar Avuha questioned him. Shimi, his son, was sharp. Chiyya appeared before Shmuel: Arakhin 16b. Shmuel said to him, “Torah scholar, I will tell you in your father’s name”: Berakhot 12a, near the end; Chagigah 14a, beginning.
